These files are preparation assets, not generic documentation. September 2026 is a **stacked HAL → IOCL campaign** — treat `combined-HAL-then-IOCL-plan.md` as the single operational source of truth.

- Keep the most actionable material near the top: exam status, timelines, source links, daily plans, question banks, or mock strategy. For HAL/IOCL, the day-by-day sprint in `combined-HAL-then-IOCL-plan.md` supersedes older sprint files.
- Use reusable subject notes in `Notes/Shared-Core/` and `Notes/{DBMS,DSA,OS,CN}/` for the conceptual base; keep exam folders (`HAL/`, `IOCL/`, `ISRO/`, `CONCOR/`) focused on framing, prioritization, and exam-specific gaps. Do not duplicate shared-core content into exam folders.
- HAL → IOCL stacking: ~73% of IOCL (75 Tech + 25 Non-Tech) is pre-covered by HAL sprint. ~27 marks (Cloud/DevOps, OOP/Web, network security, NoSQL/Linux, Quant+DI) are IOCL-only Delta Week (08–13 Sept). COA/Digital Logic/TOC/Compiler are HAL-terminal — park after 06 Sept.
- In every research-oriented file, separate `Confirmed` facts (advert, portal, admit card, syllabus PDF) from `Inferred` guidance (pattern, overlap, strategy) — never mix without labeling.
- When using content from `Resume-Berkadia.tex`, keep career details accurate (STMicro + Berkadia + UCO Bank DIT) and do not invent project numbers or role scope.
- Prefer compact tables, bullet lists, and checklists over long explanatory prose. Every drill file must have timed targets (HAL: 56s/Q, IOCL: 72s/Q).
- Log every wrong answer into `HAL/ERROR-LOG.md` with error class (`concept`/`computation`/`trap`/`time`/`misread`) and grow `HAL/FORMULA-CARD.md` daily — these roll forward into IOCL via the Stacking Ledger.
